terms.grammar: deponent verb, fourth conjugation, with the dative
evidence: Plaut. Bacch. 3.4.19; Cas. 3.3.22: virīs aliēnīs (Lewis & Short: ante-classical)

terms.gloss: a flirt (a man), one who jumps from love to love
evidence: Ov. Am. 1.3.15: dēsultor amōris, an inconstant lover (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Literally a circus rider who leaped from one horse to another (Lewis & Short); Ovid’s dēsultor amōris is the man who leaps from love to love.
Literally “a roving girl”. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 316.
